nodes.label: Sidebar with 48 px rows, collapse toggle in page header
nodes.norm_label: sidebar with 48 px rows, collapse toggle in page header
nodes.rationale: The Collapse entry was a menu item leading nowhere; collapsed, each entry is its icon centred with the name in the tooltip (half a letter peeked out until 2026-09-24).

nodes.label: only_if_table_free guard (open the table only if still free)
nodes.norm_label: only_if_table_free guard (open the table only if still free)
nodes.rationale: Dine-in with a table_id only: an open dine-in order on the table answers 409 table_has_open_order with order_id and order_number, a table that no longer exists 409 table_not_found; nothing is written under the key, so the caller can send the same dishes to POST /orders/:id/items with a key of its own. The handheld sends it on every order it opens.

nodes.label: POST /api/orders/:id/items (append to an open order)
nodes.rationale: Items take the same shape as on create; any waiter may append to any open order and the order keeps the user_id of whoever opened it; a completed or cancelled order refuses new items with order_closed.

nodes.label: Order route refusal codes (invalid_item, insufficient_stock, order_closed, table_has_open_order, table_not_found, idempotency_conflict)
nodes.norm_label: order route refusal codes (invalid_item, insufficient_stock, order_closed, table_has_open_order, table_not_found, idempotency_conflict)
nodes.rationale: Refusals carry a code a client can act on: invalid_item (400) for a dish, add-on, quantity or price the order cannot take, insufficient_stock (409), order_closed (400), order_not_found (404), table_has_open_order and table_not_found (409), idempotency_conflict (409).

nodes.label: Unsigned Windows NSIS Installer
nodes.rationale: Post-2023 CA/Browser Forum rules put code-signing keys on hardware tokens or cloud HSMs, so signing needs a signing-service integration (e.g. SignPath); the build warns but never fails. NSIS only: no Partner Center account for AppX and electron-updater ignores AppX.

nodes.label: Authentication rate limit (10 requests / 15 min per address)
nodes.norm_label: authentication rate limit (10 requests / 15 min per address)
nodes.rationale: Shared by every authentication route, and by creating or changing a staff account.

nodes.label: Per-account order route rate limits (60 writes, 120 reads a minute)
nodes.norm_label: per-account order route rate limits (60 writes, 120 reads a minute)
nodes.rationale: Counted per signed-in account because the handhelds all reach the API from 127.0.0.1 through the Server App, and counted per address they shared one budget with each other and the till.

nodes.label: Ordina: table heads the ticket, compact tiles counted on grid width
nodes.norm_label: ordina: table heads the ticket, compact tiles counted on grid width
nodes.rationale: Columns counted on the space the grid really has, not the window, because the ticket takes 320-384 px and one column too many truncates every name.

nodes.label: Product form still asks supermarket fields (SKU, barcode, cost, stock)
nodes.norm_label: product form still asks supermarket fields (sku, barcode, cost, stock)

nodes.label: Hand-written RTL check lists
nodes.rationale: The RTL test lists are written by hand: a new interface file must be added or it is not checked.

nodes.label: Page zoom on small screens (webPreferences.zoomFactor)
nodes.rationale: Even with the right window the UI, designed at ~1140x800, came out a size too large on the 1024x768 till; zoom 90% there, 5% steps, never under 75% so a 44 px button stays at the 40 px Windows touch minimum.

nodes.label: GET /api/products/:id/image (tokenless dish photo)
nodes.rationale: The one route the Server App serves without a token: the dish photo for the menu's img, open for the same reason as on :3001 and passed through byte for byte with its ETag.

nodes.norm_label: per-item and per-order discounts, new total included

nodes.label: Security & Dependency Review Job
nodes.rationale: Runs only on pull requests; fails on high severity dependency vulnerabilities.

nodes.label: End-to-End Playwright & Release Regression Job
nodes.rationale: Runs test:release-regressions with REQUIRE_VISUAL_EVIDENCE and Playwright tests; uploads playwright-report and regression evidence.

nodes.label: Sharded Core Test Suite Job
nodes.rationale: npm test (~90 suites serially, ~3.5 min) dominated the PR critical path; two round-robin shards run on separate runners in parallel with lint/build. Separate runners are required because several auth suites interfere when run concurrently. Suite list is derived from package.json's test script so shards cannot drift.

nodes.label: Windows Uninstaller Pester Tests Job
nodes.rationale: Deliberately skips npm ci: Pester is preinstalled and the driver script only uses node:path and node:child_process; npm ci cost 165s of a 5-minute budget and sometimes cancelled the whole run.

nodes.label: Release Notes from CHANGELOG.md
nodes.rationale: GitHub's PR-based generated notes came back empty because the repo pushed straight to main; a CHANGELOG entry is mandatory and the step fails loudly without one.

nodes.label: Release Tag Validation (strict X.Y.Z = package.json)
nodes.rationale: The '[0-9]*' tag glob matches malformed tags; every step reads VERSION from package.json, so a mismatched tag would silently publish a wrongly named release (issue #220).

nodes.label: Windows Auto-Update Assets (latest.yml + .exe.blockmap)
nodes.rationale: electron-updater's NSIS updater needs latest.yml and the blockmap; verification fails loudly instead of shipping a release nothing can auto-update from.

nodes.label: Floor table panel as 672 px SidePanel
nodes.norm_label: floor table panel as 672 px sidepanel
nodes.rationale: On a wide screen the room stays visible beside it; at 1024 px only a strip remains under the shadow, so there it is effectively a window.

nodes.label: Giornata orders as a list opening the shared order panel
nodes.norm_label: giornata orders as a list opening the shared order panel
nodes.rationale: Each order used to be a full panel with all its actions in a grid: a wall.

nodes.rationale: user_id is never read from the body: the order is stamped with the authenticated caller; add-on names and prices are resolved from the catalog and client-supplied ones ignored.

nodes.label: insertOrderItemRows() unified row writer
nodes.rationale: The row-writing loop was copied in order creation and item append; unified before the menu expansion became one more thing to keep aligned by hand (likewise cartItemToPayload in the UI).

nodes.label: Interrupted send replay through the send queue
nodes.norm_label: interrupted send replay through the send queue
nodes.rationale: Key and body are written on the phone before the request leaves and every repeat resends them identical; the backend answers with what it already did. The order to open or append to is decided at the tap and only the backend changes it (409 on an already open table).

nodes.label: Queue entry frozen at the tap (idempotency key, address, body)
nodes.norm_label: queue entry frozen at the tap (idempotency key, address, body)
nodes.rationale: Every repeat resends the same key, address and body; the backend keeps every answered key (order_idempotency, no expiry) and replays its answer before any other check, also for a new order since 2026-10-08, because a dish disabled meanwhile made it answer 400 to an order that existed.

nodes.label: Full Cross-Platform Matrix Workflow
nodes.rationale: Manual-only (workflow_dispatch): building linux-x64, macos-x64, macos-arm64 and windows-x64 is minutes-expensive for a fork that ships Windows; nightly cron and push-to-main triggers were spent on builds nobody looked at. better-sqlite3 >= v13 prebuilds avoid native cross-compilation.

nodes.label: Cloud Bridge & Telemetry Removal (4.0.0, migration v80)
nodes.norm_label: cloud bridge & telemetry removal (4.0.0, migration v80)
nodes.rationale: The cloud bridge that registered the installation with a vendor dashboard and the anonymous telemetry beside it were removed in 4.0.0 (service, outbox tables, settings and stored credentials alike); migration v80 clears them from existing databases and restoring an old backup does not bring them back.

nodes.label: Data Protection (pre-migration backups, restore, health checks)
nodes.norm_label: data protection (pre-migration backups, restore, health checks)
nodes.rationale: A timestamped backup is taken automatically before every schema migration; the database and local backups live in the operating-system user-data directory, separate from the installed binaries, and survive in-place updates, though a manual backup is advised before reinstalling or moving machines.

nodes.label: Optional Google Drive Backup
nodes.rationale: Reaches the network only once the owner configures and enables it, and fails gracefully when offline.

nodes.label: In-App Update Check (this repository's GitHub releases)
nodes.norm_label: in-app update check (this repository's github releases)
nodes.rationale: Besides the owner-enabled Google Drive backup, the update check against this repository's own releases is the only thing that reaches the network; in-app updates work from the first install on.

nodes.rationale: Still in the code but switched off by WHATSAPP_AVAILABLE in main/features.ts and frontend/src/lib/features.ts: no screen offers it and its service never starts.

nodes.rationale: States that an open feature request is not approval of a technical implementation.

nodes.label: Pull Request Template
nodes.rationale: Requires related work, scope, verification commands, and a compatibility & data safety section (DB impact, migration, offline/network impact).

nodes.label: Data Safety Invariant
nodes.rationale: Existing customer data must survive upgrades: never reset, truncate or drop user databases as a shortcut for migration design.

nodes.label: Offline-First Operation Invariant
nodes.rationale: Core POS operation (orders, billing, tables and service days, kitchen tickets, printing) must work without internet. The cloud bridge and usage telemetry were removed with the settings that armed them (migration v80). Only owner-configured features (Google Drive backup; WhatsApp kept in code but switched off by WHATSAPP_AVAILABLE) and the update check against the fork's own GitHub releases may reach the network, and all must fail gracefully offline. No outbound channel to a vendor may be reintroduced.

nodes.label: Scope Discipline
nodes.rationale: Implement only the approved task; no opportunistic refactors across unrelated files; adjacent issues go in the report.

nodes.label: Maintainer Approval Before Architectural Work
nodes.rationale: An open issue is not approval; features, schema changes, auth, table/service-day/reservation semantics (shaped around one restaurant), i18n architecture and large refactors need an explicit maintainer comment first, to avoid wasted effort.

nodes.label: BuonApp Does Not Talk to a Vendor
nodes.norm_label: buonapp does not talk to a vendor
nodes.rationale: Cloud bridge and anonymous telemetry removed in 4.0.0 and will not return; network features must be owner-enabled and fail gracefully offline.

nodes.label: Versioned Migrations via PRAGMA user_version
nodes.rationale: Every schema change gets a new integer migration in main/db.ts, verified on fresh and upgraded databases; destructive changes need approval, a preservation strategy and rollback plan.

nodes.label: Windows-Only Published Releases
nodes.rationale: Signing and store credentials the fork does not have used to fail the release job and take the Windows installer down with them; macOS and Linux still build from source. The Windows installer is not code-signed, so SmartScreen asks once (More info, Run anyway).

nodes.label: POST /api/auth/login (JWT, rememberMe)
nodes.rationale: rememberMe makes the token last 10 days instead of 24 hours; tenants always holds the one local business, which the frontend selects on its own.

nodes.label: KDS and Server App login routes (role-gated)
nodes.norm_label: kds and server app login routes (role-gated)
nodes.rationale: The KDS admits chef, manager and owner and returns station_ids with a 24-hour token; the Server App admits only server, with remember_me for 10 days; neither counts failed attempts, bound only by the shared authentication rate limit.

nodes.label: Login lockout (5 attempts, 15 minutes)
nodes.rationale: attempts_remaining counts down the 5 attempts allowed per address; the fifth failure carries lockout_minutes 15 and further attempts answer 429 until the time is up.

nodes.label: Role-based access (owner, manager, cashier, server, chef)
nodes.norm_label: role-based access (owner, manager, cashier, server, chef)

nodes.label: Staff user management (/api/users, /api/staff)
nodes.rationale: Owner or manager token; a manager manages only operational staff (cashier, server, chef), only an owner changes roles, and the last active owner can be neither demoted nor deactivated; a new password or PIN ends the account's open sessions.

nodes.label: Staff Roles, Username Sign-in & Manager PIN Overrides
nodes.norm_label: staff roles, username sign-in & manager pin overrides
nodes.rationale: Owner, Manager, Cashier, Server and Chef sign in with a username and a password, not an email, since nothing in BuonApp sends mail; manager PIN overrides cover voids and cancellations, and a print log is kept per bill.

nodes.label: Backend Authority Invariant
nodes.rationale: Security-critical and payment calculations remain backend-authoritative.

nodes.label: Staff accounts deactivated, never deleted
nodes.rationale: Orders and print logs refer to staff accounts, so accounts are deactivated instead of deleted.

nodes.label: Username-based login (migration v96)
nodes.rationale: BuonApp sends no mail, so an email was only an invented identifier; migration v96 turned each one into the part before the @. The username is matched regardless of case, surrounding spaces and accents, and stored lowercase with accents folded.

nodes.label: Back button through browser history (handheld-history.ts)
nodes.rationale: The Android edge gesture used to leave the page. Table, Ordina and the open ticket are history entries: back closes ticket to menu, menu to table, table to Sala, and leaves only from Sala. Entries are pushed only from a tap (Chrome skips those added without) and through Next's pushState so they carry its __NA marker, without which Next reloads; windows over a screen are not in history.

nodes.label: Touch targets 44/48/56 px
nodes.rationale: The central PC is an old touch cash monitor used mostly with a finger; the handheld is a phone: no hover-only affordances, less text, status written in words as well as colour.

nodes.label: createWindow sized to workAreaSize (1024x768 cash screen)
nodes.norm_label: createwindow sized to workareasize (1024x768 cash screen)
nodes.rationale: Requesting 1400x900 regardless left the till showing the top-left corner of a larger render; the 768 minimum height pushed the status bar and Esci under the taskbar.

nodes.label: Server App proxy allowlist (main/server-app.ts)
nodes.rationale: Forwards to :3001 only the listed GET/POST/PATCH/PUT routes and answers 404 for anything else under /api (before, an unknown route fell into the static fallback and returned the page HTML with 200). The role is checked twice: by the proxy, which admits only server, and by the main API behind every forward.

nodes.label: Unauthenticated product image passthrough with ETag
nodes.norm_label: unauthenticated product image passthrough with etag
nodes.rationale: An cannot carry a token; the main API already leaves the same route open (main/server.ts) on all interfaces, so the passthrough only brings the bytes onto the page origin allowed by its CSP (img-src 'self' data:). Bytes pass as bytes with ETag/304, read-only, 404 when the Server App is off, the main API alone decides the allowed formats (never SVG), and dot-only ids are rejected because they would vanish from the forwarded URL.

nodes.label: isPendingKot (lib/kot.ts)
nodes.rationale: The three UI counts of what is still to send (map, panel, table card) excluded different things; all now pass through one predicate, which also leaves void_adjustment rows out.

nodes.norm_label: ticket sectioned by service run (## 1a uscita / ## 2a uscita)

nodes.norm_label: ticket header and footer (table, covers, time, round, station; lines, pieces, order number)
nodes.rationale: Table and covers print large for the pass; the header names the station (Cucina) the rows were routed to; identical dishes fold into one line with the quantity summed, and the footer totals lines and pieces.

nodes.norm_label: order rows (table, time, al tavolo, in sospeso, da inviare, non pagato, total)

nodes.norm_label: per-line service run dropdown (1a uscita, 2a uscita)

nodes.norm_label: booked table tile writes booking name and party/seats (5/6) at every size
nodes.rationale: Fitted to the till's 1024x768, every table of the restaurant's 1800x1100 room was drawn below the size at which a tile wrote its booking, so a booked table only turned orange. The text shrinks first (table name down to 11 px, booking down to 10) and only then is the name cut at its end; widths are measured in the page's own font rather than guessed from the letter count. The booking time is on the booking sheet, no longer on the map.

nodes.label: Change table / Take off this table on a booked table's card
nodes.norm_label: change table / take off this table on a booked table's card
nodes.rationale: A party asking for another table is an everyday thing, and moving a booking meant going to the booking sheet. Change table picks the booking up so the next table tapped on the map takes it (a swap when that table is booked too, the row above the map saying 'Tap the new table for Rossi' with Cancel as the way out, a tap on its own table changing nothing); Take off this table sends it back to the bookings still to seat. Edit booking and Cancel booking moved into the same box, the card's foot keeping what concerns the table itself. Both go through the sheet's own POST /api/reservations/:id/assign.

nodes.label: Back to the floor from the booking sheet
nodes.norm_label: back to the floor from the booking sheet
nodes.rationale: Back to the floor sits where the floor has Bookings, and the sidebar keeps Floor lit while the sheet is open.

nodes.label: Service map fitted to the tables, not the walls
nodes.norm_label: service map fitted to the tables, not the walls
nodes.rationale: The empty edges of a room shrank every table with them. Service now frames where the tables stand plus a margin, so the restaurant's room is drawn about a fifth bigger; edit mode still shows the whole room, where tables get dragged to.

nodes.label: Small table size removed (migration v98)
nodes.rationale: A table drawn at 110 units had no room on the till for its booking under its name. The size picker offers Medium, Large and Banquet, and a two-top is drawn medium. Migration v98 makes the tables still that size medium (150x110 lying down, 110x150 standing, 140 across if round), growing from the corner they are placed by, and does the same to the tables of saved floor plans so that applying one cannot bring a small table back.

nodes.label: Bookings still to seat take the legend's place in the rooms row
nodes.norm_label: bookings still to seat take the legend's place in the rooms row
nodes.rationale: Their own band over the map cost it 113 px on the till exactly while bookings were being placed. They now sit in the rooms row on one line that scrolls sideways (chips like 'Verdi · 3', the row saying '2 to seat'), and the colour legend comes back once all are seated.

nodes.label: Release 6.5.0 - booked tables named on the map, joined tables and small size removed
nodes.norm_label: release 6.5.0 - booked tables named on the map, joined tables and small size removed

nodes.label: Held orders (/api/held-orders)
nodes.rationale: DELETE consumes a held order only when heldOrderId matches the current row, so an already-consumed or replaced row is never deleted and the table is not released by a stale request.

nodes.label: Reports summary and sales (UTC dates)
nodes.rationale: The owner dashboard is gone; a service day's close summary is where a restaurant reads its numbers, and what remains is the money read side over UTC date ranges.

nodes.label: Rooms endpoints (/api/rooms)
nodes.rationale: A room is not deleted while it still holds tables (409 room_not_empty), rather than scattering a floor plan or deleting the tables behind one click.

nodes.label: Tables endpoints (/api/tables)
nodes.rationale: Deleting a table is real and history survives through each order's table_label/room_label snapshot; it is refused with 409 table_has_open_order or table_has_held_cart while something live still points at it.

nodes.label: Giornata screen (current service day, not calendar day)
nodes.norm_label: giornata screen (current service day, not calendar day)
nodes.rationale: At one in the morning the evening's orders must stay here, not vanish into the archive while the room is still full.

nodes.label: Map MIN_SCALE 0.7 with overflow scroll
nodes.rationale: At 0.45 a four-top on a medium room at 1024 px was drawn at 74.8 px against the 76 needed for the second line, so the euro total vanished from every table. A round table asks 96 px. For huge rooms the honest answer is a list like the handheld's, not a scale tweak.

nodes.label: Sala: room selector, legend yielding to bookings, status-band tiles
nodes.norm_label: sala: room selector, legend yielding to bookings, status-band tiles
nodes.rationale: Rooms as a segmented selector, a colour legend that gives way to bookings still to place, tiles with a status band, written label and 'N da inviare' badge; a booked table writes the booking name and party over seats.

nodes.label: Booked tile: booking name and party/seats on two lines
nodes.norm_label: booked tile: booking name and party/seats on two lines
nodes.rationale: Every booked table writes the booking's name and under it the party against the seats (e.g. 4/6 with the people icon) at any size. Text shrinks first (table name to 11 px, booking to 10 px), only then is the name truncated; widths are measured in the page's font, not guessed from name length.

nodes.label: Booking sheet: assignment as exchange of places
nodes.norm_label: booking sheet: assignment as exchange of places
nodes.rationale: POST /reservations/:id/assign is the only operation: the booking takes the table and whatever was there inherits what the booking had. Assign, reassign, swap and unassign all fall out of one rule; the response names who was displaced because an invisible swap reads as a bug. Refused for a booking no longer 'booked' and onto a table that is serving. A booking with no table is the normal starting state; no_show frees a table during service, distinct from expired at close.

nodes.label: Change table / Take off the table on a booked table's panel
nodes.norm_label: change table / take off the table on a booked table's panel
nodes.rationale: A party asking for another table is an everyday thing. Change table (Cambia tavolo) picks the booking up so the next table tapped on the map takes it (a swap if that one is booked too; the strip says so, Cancel drops it); Take off the table (Togli dal tavolo) sends it back to the strip.

nodes.label: Day close ritual
nodes.rationale: Blocks on open orders or unpaid bills; owner may force with a recorded reason, which cancels orders still open so none outlives its day on a table that reads free. Freezes the summary before resetting, snapshots the layout, optionally prints the closing report, resets the room and optionally wipes the map.

nodes.label: Joined tables (tables.merged_into, v77) - removed in v97
nodes.norm_label: joined tables (tables.merged_into, v77) - removed in v97
nodes.rationale: REMOVED by migration v97. merged_into pointed a folded table at its group leader, which took the order; it gave the floor a second kind of table that took no order, no booking and no covers of its own. The owner seats a large party by changing the map in edit mode instead (a bigger table, more seats). v97 broke up standing groups, dropped the index and column, and removed POST /tables/:id/merge and /split.

nodes.label: Map service and edit-layout modes
nodes.rationale: One page, two modes: Service (read-only, tap a table to open its order, frame fitted to the tables) and Edit layout (drag, add, delete; owner/manager only; shows the whole room). No new dependency: absolutely-positioned elements with pointer events and grid snapping. Edit mode is also how a large party is seated now that joining tables is gone.

nodes.label: resolveOrderTable()
nodes.rationale: Single place answering which table an order was served at: prefers the live row, falls back to the label snapshot, so a reprint still names a table that no longer exists.

nodes.label: Rooms entity and floor map (v75)
nodes.rationale: Rooms replace free-text floor; rooms are laid out in abstract units and scaled to the frame so the same map reads on the central PC and on a tablet. Migration lays every table on a grid because position_x/position_y had never been written.

nodes.label: Service days business-day cycle (v74)
nodes.rationale: service_days with a partial unique index enforcing one open day; orders.service_day_id stamped at creation makes a day's orders an exact query. Bills are not stamped: joining through orders is exact and cannot desynchronise. Per-day summaries only; no cross-day reporting by owner's choice.

nodes.label: Service view cropped to the tables' bounding box
nodes.norm_label: service view cropped to the tables' bounding box
nodes.rationale: In service the map is fitted to where the tables stand plus a margin, rather than to the room's empty edges; the restaurant's room is drawn about a fifth bigger. Edit mode still shows the whole room.

nodes.label: Shared table geometry (main/lib/table-geometry.ts)
nodes.rationale: Default sizes from seat count and the grid placer live in one module so the migration and the routes cannot disagree about what a table looks like.

nodes.label: Saved floor plans (table_layouts, v78)
nodes.rationale: Named saved maps; applying one rebuilds the floor in one transaction through the safe delete path. Plans store names rather than ids so they survive the map being wiped: the answer to the daily tax the close ritual creates.

nodes.label: Three surfaces, one operation (sheet, map strip, table panel)
nodes.norm_label: three surfaces, one operation (sheet, map strip, table panel)
nodes.rationale: Bookings are moved from three places that all use the same assign operation: the /reservations page (list by time, single-row add, table picker showing who holds each table), the strip of unseated bookings on the map (tap one, tap a table), and the card of a booked table.

nodes.label: On the till's screen: booked tables legible at 1024x768
nodes.norm_label: on the till's screen: booked tables legible at 1024x768
nodes.rationale: A booked table used to turn orange and nothing more: fitted to the till's 1024x768, every table in the 1800x1100 room was drawn below the size at which a tile wrote its booking. Four changes were measured on that room: booked tile text, unseated chips in the legend row, service view fitted to the tables, and the small size removed.

nodes.label: Unseated booking chips replace the colour legend in the rooms row
nodes.norm_label: unseated booking chips replace the colour legend in the rooms row
nodes.rationale: Instead of a band over the map that cost it 113 px while bookings were being placed, unseated bookings sit on one sideways-scrolling line where the legend was. Chips read 'Verdi · 3': the time is on the sheet, not on the map.

nodes.label: Navigazione a cinque voci (Sala, Ordina, Giornata, Menu, Archivio)
nodes.norm_label: navigazione a cinque voci (sala, ordina, giornata, menu, archivio)
nodes.rationale: Each item answers a different question (where are they sitting / I'm taking an order / what is open now / what do I sell / what did I take in); the sidebar used to mix eleven work and configuration items.

nodes.label: Denormalized table labels (orders.table_label / room_label, v73)
nodes.rationale: Orders carry their own snapshot of where they were served, so table_id can be set to NULL on delete; history becomes self-contained and genuine table deletion becomes possible, which the rest of the design depends on.

nodes.label: getOrOpenServiceDay auto-open
nodes.rationale: An offline-first till must never refuse an order because nobody pressed a button that morning: placing an order opens a day in the tenant timezone if none is running.

nodes.label: Horizontal/vertical toggle instead of rotation
nodes.rationale: Free-angle rotation costs a fiddly editor handle; a table standing on its end is the same rectangle with width and height swapped. Orientation is read back from the stored size (taller than wide = vertical) rather than duplicated in a column. The planned rotation and notes columns were dropped.

nodes.label: Walk-in seats the wrong booking; POST /reservations/:id/reopen
nodes.norm_label: walk-in seats the wrong booking; post /reservations/:id/reopen
nodes.rationale: Any order on a held table seats its booking, so a walk-in on a reserved table closes the wrong one. Reopen puts the booking back on the sheet with no table. The owner chose this over a confirmation prompt in the POS.

nodes.label: Reservations for the current service only (v76)
nodes.norm_label: reservations for the current service only (v76)
nodes.rationale: Bookings are for the service being run now, not future dates: the room is rebuilt daily and tables are really deleted, so 'table 12 on Saturday' names something that does not exist yet. Name and guests required; time and phone optional. tables.status='reserved' is what having a booking looks like, not something a caller can assert.

nodes.label: Services own domain, routes only speak HTTP
nodes.norm_label: services own domain, routes only speak http
nodes.rationale: Table lifecycle helpers moved from main/routes/tables.ts to main/services/tables.ts because reservations needed the service day and the day close needed table deletion, making route and service import each other in a circle; no import cycles remain in main/.

nodes.label: Table size presets: medium, large, banquet (small removed, v98)
nodes.norm_label: table size presets: medium, large, banquet (small removed, v98)
nodes.rationale: Tables cannot be resized by a drag handle; size comes from three presets. Migration v98 removed the small size: tables and saved plans still that size became medium, keeping their orientation, and a two-top now defaults to medium, so a tile is big enough to write its booking on the till's 1024x768 screen.

nodes.label: Order item cancel / void (void_adjustment)
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.rationale: An item in preparing or ready is voided with a negative void_adjustment bill line and a manager PIN instead of restoring stock; on a fixed menu cancelling the package row takes the whole menu off the check and a dish row only that dish, and restore follows the same split.

nodes.label: cancelTargetIds split cancel (package vs dish)
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.rationale: The package row is the menu and cancelling it removes everything; a dish row is only itself, so changing one's mind on the main does not lose the starter already eaten; restore follows the same rule.

nodes.label: compactKotItems / compactBillRows / compactOrderRows
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.rationale: 'Lasagne 3' is only how identical portions are shown: compactKotItems on the ticket, compactBillRows on the preconto and compactOrderRows on the table screens; since 2026-09-24 they also sum a la carte dishes added in several rounds.

nodes.label: fixed_menu_course_products per-dish exceptions (v93)
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.rationale: Exceptions both ways (a dish in the category but not in the menu, or outside it and in); explicit beats category. A separate table because SQLite cannot add a column with CHECK and the editor prunes surcharges.

nodes.label: Menu fisso (fixed menu as a product)
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.norm_label: menu fisso (fixed menu as a product)
nodes.rationale: A fixed menu is a product with a flag, inheriting order rows, bill, archive and reports for free; courses, course categories and surcharges hang around it.

nodes.label: FixedMenuPicker window (counted menu)
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.rationale: Takes catalogue and menu as props and returns the selection with a callback on the AddonModal model, with no API client, which makes it mountable in the handheld Server App. Every number on it counts dishes: a course shows '3 di 8' in amber while short and red when over, and a full course greys out its other dishes and flashes 'Al completo'.

nodes.label: Menu a conteggio (counted fixed menu)
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.rationale: At the table one asks how many take the menu and then counts dishes course by course; one group with the menu row at quantity N, dishes still one row per portion, shown compacted. Chosen over quantity rows to avoid splitting rows when one portion changes run or gets a note.

nodes.label: order_items.menu_course_id (v95)
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.rationale: Says which course a row satisfies; deducing it from the category stopped working once a course takes a dish from outside its categories or two courses share one; backfilled only where exactly one course matches.

nodes.label: order_items.menu_group_id and menu_role
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.rationale: menu_role (package or course) lets each row say what it is without a join to products, the same reason product_name is copied on the row; two menus at one table are two groups.

nodes.label: PATCH /orders/:id/menu-groups/:groupId { quantity }
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.rationale: Changes how many menus a line holds, for the friend who arrives late; below the dishes already in a course it answers 409 menu_course_overflow naming the course; same roles and checks as the fill and in the handheld allowlist; removing the menu row removes all N menus.

nodes.label: NOT_A_MENU_PACKAGE KDS filter (services/kds.ts)
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.rationale: The KDS reads the same rows as the ticket, so the package would have appeared as a dish to cook; the ticket filter sits in routeItemsToStations so the package row still receives its kot_batch stamp.

nodes.label: Menu aperto: a container that fills (v95)
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.norm_label: menu aperto: a container that fills (v95)
nodes.rationale: A required course may stay empty since the price sits on the package. The rejected alternative was declaring only how many menus and guessing the attribution, which would change what the guest pays whenever it guesses wrong.

nodes.label: planCourseFill matching
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.rationale: A bare id keeps the row's note and run, so a 'no salt' soup is not cancelled and rewritten; the most precise requests match first (note and run, then note, then bare ids), and rows already in the kitchen before pending ones, so removing one lasagna of three frees a pending one instead of a 409.

nodes.label: Prodotto Generico with "prezzo da definire"
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.rationale: The signal sits on the product and not on a zero price, because amari and coffee are almost always offered and a value-based warning would always be lit.

nodes.label: "Offerto" label on preconto for zero rows
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.norm_label: "offerto" label on preconto for zero rows

nodes.label: pendingDishCount (counts dishes not rows)
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte

nodes.label: Fixed Menus (counted, one price)
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.rationale: Rung up the way the floor writes it on the pad: how many menus, then how many of each dish, without asking who eats what. One line carries the number and the price; under it the menu writes real rows, one per portion, so the kitchen ticket sections them by category and a portion can carry its own note, written once for all the plates that share it, while the bill folds identical ones into 'Lasagne 3'. A menu that includes the cover takes its guests off the cover charge; cancelling the menu row removes the whole menu, cancelling a dish only that dish.

nodes.label: Fixed menu writes real order rows
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.norm_label: fixed menu writes real order rows
nodes.rationale: An addon group item has no category, and the kitchen ticket sections by product category, so a package built on addons reached the kitchen undivided. The menu writes one real row per chosen dish; the price stays on the package row.

nodes.label: Renderer loading page (index.html)
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server

nodes.label: Health-check redirect to localhost:3001
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server

nodes.label: mDNS advertisement buonapp.local
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server

nodes.label: PUT /orders/:id/menu-groups/:groupId/courses/:courseId
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server
nodes.rationale: product_ids is what the course holds afterwards, so one endpoint adds, swaps and clears and replaying the same list changes nothing; new rows are born with kot_batch NULL and go out on the next round; a dish the kitchen has already started returns 409 course_in_progress and nothing is written.

nodes.label: POST /api/printers/print-kot
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server
nodes.rationale: Only never-sent rows go out, stamped with the next round and routed to the kitchen stations; batch re-prints a round without a new number; nothing pending answers 200 printed:false; servers may call it because on a handheld sending the order is firing the ticket, while print-bill stays closed to them.

nodes.label: Server App for handhelds (:3003)
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server

nodes.label: PATCH /orders/:id/items/:itemId/service-run
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server
nodes.rationale: Any waiter on any order, and no manager PIN since no money moves. Runs are labels, not gates: kot_batch is deliberately untouched, so a row already printed still moves and nothing is re-sent.

nodes.label: Standalone KDS server (:3002)
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server
nodes.rationale: Enabled by default; with kds_enabled switched off, /api/kds-info, /api/kitchen/* and /api/kds/* answer 403.

nodes.label: useSyncServerLanguage for standalone surfaces
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server

nodes.label: Palmari sidebar item (QR modal)
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server

nodes.label: Handheld web manifest and safe-area layout
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server
nodes.norm_label: handheld web manifest and safe-area layout
nodes.rationale: The route layout declares viewport-fit=cover and its own public/server-app.webmanifest starting from /server-standalone instead of the till, so added to the home screen it opens on the room; header and action bar keep clear of notch and home indicator with env(safe-area-inset-*).

nodes.label: Known limits of the handheld (Cosa resta fuori)
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server
nodes.norm_label: known limits of the handheld (cosa resta fuori)
nodes.rationale: Two waiters on the same menu: the PUT is last-writer-wins. The till can still open a second order on an occupied table, since only the handheld sends only_if_table_free. The handheld token expires at a fixed time (10 days with Ricordami, 24 h without) and is not renewed, though ticket and queue survive. The PC keeps the same single-attempt trap in append-attempt.ts. The cart estimate excludes the cover charge, which the backend computes.

nodes.label: Kitchen ticket per order at end of queue round (45 s timeout)
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server
nodes.norm_label: kitchen ticket per order at end of queue round (45 s timeout)
nodes.rationale: The kitchen ticket leaves at the end of the round, one per order, from a list saved with the queue, so two waiting rounds of a table print on one sheet; without network the order stays listed for the next round and a printer error gives the usual warning. 45 s because an unplugged network printer costs 5 s per station and a USB one on Windows up to 20.

nodes.label: Legacy send attempts adopted into the queue
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server
nodes.norm_label: legacy send attempts adopted into the queue
nodes.rationale: Attempts left by the previous version (buonapp:server-app-order-attempt and the waiter's append-attempt key) enter the queue on first start with their own key, so an interrupted send from before the upgrade is neither lost nor doubled.

nodes.label: Send queue (coda d'invio) on the phone
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server
nodes.norm_label: send queue (coda d'invio) on the phone
nodes.rationale: Before, an interrupted send left a single pending attempt per waiter (lib/append-attempt.ts) and every later send, on any table, failed until a reload that threw the ticket away. Now Invia writes the ticket into a queue on the phone that sends it immediately or by itself when the link returns, one entry at a time and in order within each table, while a waiting table does not block the others.

nodes.label: Server App tableside handheld (:3003, buonapp.local)
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server
nodes.rationale: Until 5.0.0 it kept FloCafe's features (product grid, one note per line, send); the PC windows were written props-in/callbacks-out so they could be mounted here untouched. Rebuilt 2026-09-15, restyled 2026-09-16, made reliable 2026-10-08 after two service reports (phone losing the Wi-Fi and a long 20-cover ticket lost on reload).

nodes.label: ServerAppAccess QR codes (sidebar "Palmari" and Settings)
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server
nodes.rationale: Moved into the PC sidebar item "Palmari" (a modal over the current screen, so a half-taken order survives) so a cashier, who cannot see Settings, can show it to a new waiter; the QR is only an address and the waiter's credentials are still required. Hidden when server_app_enabled is off; Settings now shows the codes immediately.

nodes.label: TableScreen (full page table view with pending tickets)
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server
nodes.norm_label: tablescreen (full page table view with pending tickets)
nodes.rationale: A full page with a back arrow replaced the drawer, which had no close button and had to be unmounted whenever the menu window opened on the same layer. No service-run selector inside a fixed menu: courses already order the runs.

nodes.label: What to check when the phone loses the Wi-Fi
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server
nodes.norm_label: what to check when the phone loses the wi-fi
nodes.rationale: The handheld now survives a network gap but the network still needs care. In order: phone switching to mobile data (adaptive Wi-Fi / Wi-Fi Assist), Wi-Fi off while the screen sleeps and battery optimisation, PC changing address (reserve a DHCP address, the QR points to it, not every phone resolves buonapp.local), PC sleeping or powering down its network card and a non-private network letting the firewall close ports 3001-3003, coverage (repeater or mesh with the same SSID). Without HTTPS no service worker registers, so a reload while the PC is mute shows the browser error page.

nodes.label: SEC-01 LAN traffic not encrypted
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server

nodes.label: Express API and WebSocket Server (:3001)
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server

nodes.label: Standalone Kitchen Display Server (:3002)
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server
nodes.rationale: Optional, for kitchens that work off a screen instead of paper; it can be switched off entirely, which closes its endpoints.

nodes.label: mDNS Advertisement as buonapp.local
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server

nodes.label: Tableside Server App for Handhelds (:3003)
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server
nodes.rationale: A phone joins by scanning the code under Handhelds in the till's sidebar and signs in with a waiter's own account; it shows a read-only floor, then the menu with a stepper beside each dish and the till's own windows for extras, fixed menus and service runs. Any waiter can work any open order; sending fires the kitchen ticket exactly as the till does, and handhelds take no money and cannot change the floor.

nodes.label: Server App narrow forwarding allowlist
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server
nodes.rationale: The handheld gets only the catalogue, read-only settings, rooms and tables, the order routes a waiter needs (create, append, guests, service-run, menu-groups) and print-kot; no table write, bill, payment or customer route is forwarded, and everything else under /api answers 404.

nodes.label: Backend decides who opens the table (only_if_table_free, 409 table_has_open_order)
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server
nodes.norm_label: backend decides who opens the table (only_if_table_free, 409 table_has_open_order)
nodes.rationale: If the table was opened meanwhile (another handheld, the till, an earlier ticket of the same phone) the 409 names the open order and proves nothing was written under that key; the same dishes go onto it as an append with key <key>:a, without covers or notes, and the waiter is told when another device opened it.

nodes.label: Every waiter on every table (ownership constraint dropped)
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server
nodes.norm_label: every waiter on every table (ownership constraint dropped)
nodes.rationale: The handheld taking the main course is not the one that took the starter, so the seven ownership guards in main/routes/orders.ts and main/routes/index.ts were dropped on handheld and PC; per-route requireRole stays (a waiter still cannot discount, reprice or cash), and orders.user_id is still stamped from the token, never the body.

nodes.label: Handheld never imports @/lib/api
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server
nodes.rationale: The PC API client's 401 interceptor would send the handheld back to the PC login; the handheld uses its own server-api.ts client and writes only the currency into the PC auth store already in the bundle.

nodes.label: Keep Ports 3001-3003 on Private LAN
nodes.community_name: Doc comande, palmare e tre server
nodes.rationale: The three local servers must never be forwarded to the public internet; the OS account protects the local database and backups.

nodes.label: Discount after the check changes (percentage recomputed, euros kept)
nodes.norm_label: discount after the check changes (percentage recomputed, euros kept)
nodes.rationale: A percentage is recomputed on the new food total, while a discount in euros (amount or total) stays what was agreed and never exceeds the food left on the check.

nodes.label: New-total order discount (discount_type total, target_total)
nodes.rationale: The server works out the discount against the order as it stands under the transaction lock, so an item added meanwhile moves the discount, not the total; it is computed from the undiscounted check so a second rounding replaces the first, and it cannot go below the cover and other charges because a discount only comes off the food.

nodes.label: Discount settings (/api/settings/discount, discount_methods)
nodes.rationale: discount_methods lists the switched-on ways to discount (total, percentage, amount) in button order, never empty and without repeats; the discount window opens on the first.

nodes.label: Order, item and bill discounts with limits
nodes.norm_label: order, item and bill discounts with limits
nodes.rationale: The new total is offered only on the order discount; item and bill discounts take percentage or amount; every method must be switched on in discount_methods, and discount_requires_approval demands an override_pin.

nodes.label: Coperto (cover charge, migrations v88-v90)
nodes.rationale: (covers - covers included in a menu) x amount; takeaway pays no cover; covers are correctable on an open order via PATCH /orders/:id/guests, and the cover travels with the total in recomputeOrderAfterItemChange() so the printed line never divides an old amount by new heads.

nodes.label: coversForNewOrder (covers start from table)
nodes.rationale: A new order's covers start from the booking's party if the table is booked, otherwise from the table's seats, within 1-99. A hand-set count (guestCountChosen) sticks across table changes; an open order keeps its own covers, and appending dishes no longer shows the counter.

nodes.label: orderCoverCharge() / computeCoverCharge
nodes.rationale: Included covers count one per menu and never more than the guests (computeCoverCharge clamps at zero); recomputed in orderCoverCharge() from every point that changes rows: create, append, recompute, cancel, restore.

nodes.label: Till sidebar (Sala, Ordina, Giornata, Menu, Archivio; Palmari, Impostazioni, user, Esci)
nodes.norm_label: till sidebar (sala, ordina, giornata, menu, archivio; palmari, impostazioni, user, esci)
nodes.rationale: The screens of a service at the top and Handhelds and Settings at the foot, with the restaurant name and the signed-in user; large touch targets for a touch-monitor till.

nodes.label: Menu grid with colour-coded category chips
nodes.norm_label: menu grid with colour-coded category chips
nodes.rationale: Search plus chips Tutti, Antipasti, Primi, Secondi, Contorni, Dolci, Bevande, each in its own tint; dishes as cards with an initials tile instead of a photo, the price, a pencil for options and a blue count badge for what is already on the ticket.

nodes.label: Ticket panel (Al tavolo/Asporto, table with Cambia, covers stepper, order note, Invia ordine)
nodes.norm_label: ticket panel (al tavolo/asporto, table with cambia, covers stepper, order note, invia ordine)
nodes.rationale: Dine-in or takeaway toggle, the table with a Change button, covers adjusted with -/+, an optional order note, plate count and total, a hold button and a single Send order action: the ordering screen sends and takes no money.

nodes.label: Card actions (Aggiungi Articolo, Invia in cucina (12), Stampa preconto, Incassa)
nodes.norm_label: card actions (aggiungi articolo, invia in cucina (12), stampa preconto, incassa)
nodes.rationale: Sending, printing the preconto and cashing all happen from the card; the send button counts the dishes not yet in the kitchen.

nodes.label: Totals with the cover line (Subtotale, Coperto (4), Totale)
nodes.norm_label: totals with the cover line (subtotale, coperto (4), totale)

nodes.label: discount_methods: ogni metodo di sconto acceso da solo (migrazione v99)
nodes.norm_label: discount_methods: ogni metodo di sconto acceso da solo (migrazione v99)
nodes.rationale: Replaces the old single choice "entrambi / solo % / solo importo"; early payment still offers only percentage and amount.

nodes.label: Sconto sul conto come nuovo totale
nodes.norm_label: sconto sul conto come nuovo totale
nodes.rationale: At the restaurant a discount is almost always a rounding ("sono 53,40, facciamo 50") and the subtraction had to be done in one's head; the new total is the first method, with ready-made proposals (drop the cents, down to 5 or 10 euros), the server computes the discount in main/services/discounts.ts and the preconto prints the usual "Sconto" line; the total never drops below the cover because the discount only touches the dishes.

nodes.label: Prendi ordine from a free table (/pos?table=<id>)
nodes.norm_label: prendi ordine from a free table (/pos?table=<id>)

nodes.label: Cover Charge
nodes.rationale: A price per cover, set once, carried by every dine-in order by head count and printed on the preconto; a new order's covers start from the booking's party or the table's seats; changing the covers on an open order re-prices it, and the printed line spells out 'Cover 4 x 2,00' only when that multiplication really gives the amount.

nodes.label: Order screen screenshot (Ordina)
nodes.rationale: Two panes: the menu grid on the left and the ticket for table 7 on the right, with a printer button in the header; the page composes and sends, with no payment step.

nodes.label: Table card screenshot (Tavolo)
nodes.rationale: Table 8's card slides over the dimmed floor map: chips Occupato and '12 da inviare', room and seats, order meta (Al Tavolo, 8 minutes ago, order number, In sospeso, Non pagato), the lines, the totals and the actions.

nodes.label: orderCharges() single charge sum (main/money.ts)

nodes.norm_label: kitchen ticket layout and dish folding

Identical dishes fold unless product, add-ons, note, variants or run differ; the closing line and piece count plus order number let the pass check the ticket.

nodes.label: Service runs on kitchen tickets
nodes.rationale: A run says when a dish leaves the kitchen, distinct from the round; no send-one-run to avoid state out of step with the round. The run's # rule, in bold double height across the full paper width, is the only line drawn inside the list of dishes.

nodes.label: Connection detection and /api/health probe (connection.ts)
nodes.rationale: Any response, even a refusal, means the PC is there; no response means it is not. nodes.rationale: A note belongs to the plates it is written on, so it becomes one counted line under the dish instead of one line per plate; nothing changes on the server because the order already carried equal notes as a quantity.

nodes.label: Note line counter (light red -, plate count, light green +) before the note
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.norm_label: note line counter (light red -, plate count, light green +) before the note
nodes.rationale: + moves one of the dish's plain plates onto the note so the dish total does not move; only when every plate already has a note does it add one, if the course has room (a full course lights up as for a dish tap). - gives a plate back to the plain count and removes the line at the last, replacing the old X that removed the note.

nodes.label: Note-line counter (one note for several equal portions)
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.norm_label: note-line counter (one note for several equal portions)
nodes.rationale: The note line reads '- 2 + senza besciamella': a light red minus, how many portions carry that note, a light green plus. The plus marks another already-counted portion with the same note, or adds one when no plain portion is left and the course has room; the minus returns one to the plain count and removes the line at the last. Neither changes the dish total (the dish's own minus does that). It is smaller than the dish counter (32 px) and sits before the note because, drawn like the dish counter at the end of the row, it looked like a second count of the dish and at full size left the note half a row. Before, every noted portion was a row of its own, so three lasagne without bechamel needed the same note written three times.

nodes.label: Per-portion note icon in the dish row
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.norm_label: per-portion note icon in the dish row
nodes.rationale: The note for a single portion is the icon left of the minus, shown once the dish has at least one portion: it takes one portion from the plain count and gives it its own line under the dish with the note ('senza besciamella'). That line now carries its own small counter before the note, so one note counts several equal portions; there is no longer a cross that removes the note. The field is 16 px on the phone because the iPhone zooms the page on smaller fields.

nodes.label: printableBillRows (cancelled rows off the preconto)

nodes.rationale: A lasagna removed before reaching the kitchen printed at 10,00 above a total that did not count it; now cancelled rows stay off the bill while voided ones stay beside their negative compensating line, with one rule per printing path (main/printers/thermal.ts, and frontend/src/lib/printer/bill-rows.ts shared by the browser encoder and HTML page).

nodes.rationale: A discount agreed on the menu line scales with the number (five menus out of eight keep five eighths), since keeping it whole would leave eight menus' discount on the one left while the floor changes the count and a discount needs the manager PIN; an order discount in euros stops at what remains on the check.

nodes.label: is_required becomes «Prevista» (expected course)
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.rationale: Since a menu can be rung up half-decided, is_required no longer blocks the order: it says which courses the menu expects, i.e. what to flag if the check closes without them; a missing course is an amber row and never a refusal.

nodes.label: «Quanti menu?» count with no default
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.rationale: One stepper whose number can also be typed; it starts from no number and nothing is added without it, because with mixed tables starting from the covers would charge menus not taken. The bottom button says 'Quanti menu?' and points the finger there, and the field selects its content a frame after the tap because the iPhone ignores a selection made while the cursor arrives ('8' plus '20' became 82 menus).

nodes.label: Nothing moves under the finger (fixed-width dish row controls)
nodes.community_name: Doc menu a conteggio e righe compatte
nodes.norm_label: nothing moves under the finger (fixed-width dish row controls)
nodes.rationale: A table of twenty is counted in sixty quick taps without looking, and every growing row shifted the others so a tap landed on the next dish or on the note button (it happened on 2026-10-07). Now note, minus, number and plus keep fixed widths with the not-yet-needed ones invisible, the name changes colour rather than weight, and the footer has a fixed-height status line.

nodes.label: Discounts (percentage, flat amount, new total)
nodes.rationale: Per item or on the whole check; each of the three ways is switched on or off in Settings. The new total is what the table is told ('it's 53.40, call it 50'), with round figures to tap and the discount worked out by the server; a maximum percentage and a maximum amount cap them, a manager PIN can be required, and a discount given by mistake can be taken off.

nodes.label: Order Workflows (dine-in, takeaway, delivery)
nodes.rationale: Only the order types the house actually takes; carts held on a table and shared across devices; open-price rows. An order is drawn up, cashed and reprinted from one place (the table on the floor plan, or the day's list for takeaway and delivery); with table service the ordering screen composes and sends and takes no money, because the till is the machine beside the computer.
